title: Insured-Requested Cancellation and Return Premium — Homeowners Insurance
content:
## Cancellation by the insured

1. An insured cancellation of a Homeowners Insurance policy is effective on the date requested, never earlier than the request.
2. A cancellation is a free-look cancellation when it is effective within the program's free-look period in calendar days after the effective date. Counting starts the day after the effective date, and the last counted day qualifies.
3. A free-look cancellation, and a binder cancelled because the closing did not happen, return the full premium paid.
4. Any other insured cancellation returns the unearned premium less the program's short-rate penalty percentage of that unearned premium, but never leaves less than the program's minimum earned premium percentage of the term premium earned. The unearned premium is the term premium multiplied by the unused days and divided by the days in the term.
5. Return premium is paid within the program's refund processing period in calendar days.

On a cancellation at the insured's request, and on a binder cancelled because the closing did not happen, the return premium is credited to the insured's premium account, dated on the cancellation effective date.

## The free-look window on abstract days

The free-look check reads the policy's effective date from the agency's records for that policy, not from the insured's account of it. Take a free-look period of N calendar days and an effective date called Day 0.

| Cancellation effective on | Counted days after the effective date | Free-look cancellation |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | 1, the first counted day | Yes |
| Day N, the last counted day | N | Yes |
| Day N plus one | More than N | No |

## Return premium after the free-look period

The return premium is the unearned premium reduced by the short-rate penalty, and is limited so that the premium earned, which is the term premium less the return premium, is at least the minimum earned percentage of the term premium.

### Worked figures (all inputs hypothetical)

Inputs, chosen for illustration and not the figures of any program: a term premium of 1,825.00 dollars over a 365-day term, a short-rate penalty of 10 percent, a minimum earned premium of 25 percent.

**Case A, 146 unused days.**
- Unearned premium: 1,825.00 multiplied by 146 and divided by 365 is 730.00.
- Short-rate penalty: 10 percent of 730.00 is 73.00; return premium 730.00 less 73.00 is 657.00.
- Premium earned: 1,825.00 less 657.00 is 1,168.00, which is not less than the minimum of 25 percent of 1,825.00, that is 456.25. The return premium is 657.00 dollars.

**Case B, 330 unused days.**
- Unearned premium: 1,825.00 multiplied by 330 and divided by 365 is 1,650.00.
- Short-rate penalty: 10 percent of 1,650.00 is 165.00; 1,650.00 less 165.00 is 1,485.00.
- Premium earned would be 1,825.00 less 1,485.00, that is 340.00, which is less than 456.25. The return premium is therefore limited to 1,825.00 less 456.25, that is 1,368.75 dollars, leaving 456.25 dollars earned.

## Points of judgement

- **Effective date of an insured cancellation.** It is the date the insured requests, and it is never earlier than the date of the request.
- **Closing did not happen.** A binder cancelled because the closing did not happen returns the full premium paid, the same as a free-look cancellation.
- **Full premium paid.** On a free-look cancellation the amount returned is the full premium the insured has paid.
